posts.cooked: We have to generate key pair for SSH from windows PowerShell or from terminal of VM installed in windows?

posts.name: Anirban Roy
posts.cooked:
From Windows Powershell.

Screenshot 2026-02-11 2019561343×200 23.6 KB

You can find these instructions here.

posts.name: N
posts.cooked:
I had seen this but some senior suggested to do in VM terminal. So it would be good if any TA or Instructor clarify this.
@21f3000759

posts.name: Mrinal
posts.cooked:
Anything works. Because ultimately you will be writing your code in the course VM and not your powershell or any other VM that you may have installed. No pros or cons for both.

For new users powershell is suggested because it is pre-installed and you do not need to install/setup any extra tools to connect to the course VM.

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
Replying since you tagged me, although Mrinal has already answered it. You can check the above message.

“Windows Terminal is the modern, open-source terminal application for Windows 10/11, offering features like multiple tabs, panes, GPU-accelerated rendering, and support for PowerShell, Command Prompt, and WSL. It is pre-installed on Windows 11 and available for free from Microsoft Store” - As stated on Microsoft’s website.

So, Terminal is an app which can run Powershell, so you can use it for logging in to the VM.
